runs.name: CMS Energy Corporation; NYSE CMS, SEC CIK 0000811156, Michigan, 10-K filer jointly with its subsidiary Consumers Energy Company; parent of Consumers, an electric and gas utility, and NorthStar Clean Energy, an independent power producer and marketer, three segments (electric utility, gas utility, NorthStar Clean Energy); convertible senior notes due 2031 (November 2025), equity offering programs of $1,000,000,000 (2026-02-11) and $3,000,000,000 (2026-05-13), authorized shares raised to 700.0M, CFO succession 2026-06-03, non-utility renewables development exited 2026-07-28; the 10-K names no rival, DTE, Ameren and WEC chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$68.70** (close 2026-10-16, aggregator, flagged). Shares **313,577,136** common on the cover of the Q2 2026 10-Q (0000811156-26-000028; `Screens/cover_shares.py` agreeing; the 84,108,789 Consumers shares on the same cover all held by CMS, not added; balance sheet 313.6M), one class; market cap $21,543M; issuance after 2026-07-28 not visible, the count may be slightly low. Sovereign **5.43%**, US Treasury 30-year par yield of 2026-10-16 (issuing authority). Read from the FY2025 10-K (0000811156-26-000004), the Q2 2026 10-Q, the 2026 proxy (0000811156-26-000015), the FY2022, FY2020 and FY2017 10-Ks and the recent 8-Ks; lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file; 2025 operating cash $2,235M cross-checked to the filed cash-flow statement; `tools/run.py` printed a window ending 2022 (the capital-spending element changed), 2023 to 2025 read from the filed statements. **Q1 IN**: a Michigan rate-regulated electric and gas utility, key variables rate base growth (more than 8% a year in the 10-K, more than 10% in the 10-Q) and the allowed return (9.90% electric, 9.80% gas, against 10.25% asked), the regulatory climate carried. **Q2 IN**: electric deciding at 61% of five-year segment net income (gas 34%, NorthStar 5%); a franchised grid under one commission no attacker with money could duplicate; the commission cuts each ask (2025 electric $277M granted of $436M sought, 2024 $176M of $325M), "affordability concerns" named in Item 1A; the generation half stands on a statute, the 10% Retail Open Access cap full with a waiting list; a regulated fair return carried to Q3. **Q3 WEIGHS AGAINST**: added plant earns about 5.2% pre-tax after depreciation ($497M on $9.6B); operating cash less all capital spending negative every year 2022 to 2025; reinvestment largely compulsory. **Q4 accounts IN, habits against**: regulatory assets not building, adjusted-EPS exclusions small ($0.08); the guidance habit, the featured adjusted figure and pay on it carried to Q5. **Q5 OUT on integrity doubt**: the proxy features "23 years of meeting or exceeding our adjusted earnings guidance", the presentation draws adjusted EPS as a straight line "for over two decades, regardless of conditions" across five CEOs, 70% of the annual bonus rests on adjusted EPS, paid at 150% for 2025; the year-shaping levers visible (deferred storm expense, gain amortization "in lieu of rate relief") while normal weather is sized at minus 22 cents against a 7-cent guidance range; no misstatement found; ability weighs for. Q6 to Q12 not reached. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE, equity-only central (Q7, The regulated utility): owner cash **$682M a year** maintenance-only (2021 to 2025 average, depreciation as the stated guess, working capital counted), $379M after all spending with the debt credit ($6,781M of net debt raised, neither the 65% consolidated nor Consumers' 0.51 cap binding; $198M with the EnerBank sale proceeds left out); the series changes sign in 2022, so by (b) the central range is the no-growth case alone, **$40.08 a share equity-only**, $40.08 to $57.55 beside with the 2022 gas-price working-capital draw out of the growth measure; expected return 3.2% to 4.7% at the price, below the floor and the bond; fair price **$21.76 equity-only** ($23.92 beside); all-equity **-$26.26**, not positive. Balance sheets 2016 to mid-2026: assets $21.6B to $40.9B, long-term debt $8.6B to $18.2B, about twice equity throughout; equity $4.3B to $9.8B, shares 279.2M (2016) to 313.6M, about $750M of new equity a year planned; pre-tax interest coverage 2.6x in 2025. Competitors: none named in the 10-K; DTE (same commission), Ameren and WEC chosen as a CONVENTION, XBRL only: 2016 to 2025 return on book equity CMS about 12% to 14% (above allowed partly on parent debt), DTE 9% to 13%, Ameren 7% to 11%, WEC 11% to 13%, no year of collapse. Strongest evidence against: the guidance streak as the leading boast, paid on; cash consumed every year, each plan needing new debt and shares; the commission cutting each ask; generation protected only by the statutory cap; the price above every case. Commits 72164472 (template), 37494bda (Step 0 and Q1), 7c67ead8 (Q2), b92b4647 (Q3 and Q4), 3576e607 (Q5), 272cfa86 (box, computation, after the stop, self-audit, gaps); write-early departures declared, two questions in one commit twice. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Contamination declared: a `Test Runs/` listing filtered to 2026-10-18 made to confirm the file name was free, which printed the names of 22 other runs of that date and an ADDENDUM (none opened; a breach of the blind rule's letter, declared in the self-audit), session commit subjects and a memory line, none used. Citations: the analyst's `check_cites.py` 54 ids, 0 problems; the dispatcher's `_dispatcher_cite_check.py` no missing id, 43 adjacent quoted fragments, 11 flagged and all read: filing quotes (Item 1A, Item 7, the proxy, slide 12) or a fragment broken across a line, **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. Brief slip by the dispatcher: the company line gave the 10-K's filing date as "2026-0210" for 2026-02-10; the analyst read the right filing. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q7 (b) against (d) when the aberrational working-capital year is in the middle of the window; (2) the regulated utility's debt credit, gross or net debt raised, and whether the maintenance case takes it; (3) whose allowed debt share, the parent's consolidated or the regulated subsidiary's, when the filing states none; (4) Q5 has no stated test between a utility's designed steadiness and the make-the-numbers habit, so another reader could pass Q5 and close OUT at Q7; (5) the named-rival rule yields none for a franchise monopoly; (6) `tools/run.py` capital-spending element after 2022; (7) em dashes in the template's headings. Could not get: the commission's allowed debt share; the peers' filed statements; a filer maintenance figure; issuance after 2026-07-28. Not armed: the box is not OUT at Q7 or IN.
runs.narr: OUT at Q5 (CMS Energy Corporation, CMS; Michigan rate-regulated electric and gas utility with NorthStar Clean Energy; Q1 IN; Q2 IN, electric deciding at 61%, the commission cutting each ask, generation on a full statutory cap; Q3 against, about 5.2% pre-tax on added plant, cash consumed every year; Q4 accounts IN, habits against; Q5 OUT on integrity doubt: 23 years of meeting or exceeding adjusted EPS guidance featured in the proxy, adjusted EPS drawn as a straight line regardless of conditions, 70% of the bonus on it, no misstatement found; computation only: owner cash $682M a year equity-only maintenance-only, value $40.08 no-growth alone ($40.08 to $57.55 beside) vs $68.70, fair $21.76 equity-only, -$26.26 all-equity; no citation slip; not held; not armed; framework gaps for the operator: (b) against (d) for a middle year, gross or net debt raised in the utility credit, whose allowed debt share, no Q5 test between designed steadiness and the habit, the named-rival rule for a monopoly)
